requirements.quote:
In this scheme, an entire domain name or a list of labels at
the end of a domain name is replaced with a pointer to a prior occurance
of the same name.
requirements.condition: When compressing an entire domain name or a trailing sequence of its labels.
requirements.required_behavior: Replace the compressed name or suffix with a pointer to an occurrence of the same name or suffix.
requirements.why_checkable: Expansion of each generated pointer can be compared with the name or suffix it replaces.

requirements.quote:
In this scheme, an entire domain name or a list of labels at
the end of a domain name is replaced with a pointer to a prior occurance
of the same name.
requirements.condition: When generating a domain-name compression pointer.
requirements.required_behavior: Point to a prior occurrence of the referenced name within the message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Point to a later occurrence of the referenced name.
requirements.why_checkable: The target position can be compared with the pointer position in an encoded message.

requirements.quote: The pointer takes the form of a two octet sequence:
requirements.condition: When encoding a domain-name compression pointer.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the pointer as exactly two octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The wire representation has a directly measurable pointer length.

requirements.quote: The first two bits are ones.
requirements.condition: When encoding a domain-name compression pointer.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the first two bits to one.
requirements.why_checkable: The pointer prefix bits can be inspected in generated messages.

requirements.quote:
This allows a pointer to be distinguished
from a label, since the label must begin with two zero bits because
labels are restricted to 63 octets or less.
requirements.condition: When encoding an ordinary domain-name label.
requirements.required_behavior: Begin the label encoding with two zero bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The top two bits of an ordinary label encoding can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
This allows a pointer to be distinguished
from a label, since the label must begin with two zero bits because
labels are restricted to 63 octets or less.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the label to 63 octets or fewer.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary-length labels can be checked against the encoder and parser.

requirements.quote:
(The 10 and 01 combinations
are reserved for future use.)
requirements.condition: When interpreting the first two bits of a domain-name component.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the 10 and 01 combinations as reserved for future use.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the 10 or 01 combinations as an ordinary label or compression-pointer encoding defined by this compression scheme.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoder discriminator and generated prefix values can be inspected; no particular rejection response is specified.

requirements.quote:
The OFFSET field specifies an offset from
the start of the message (i.e., the first octet of the ID field in the
domain header).  A zero offset specifies the first byte of the ID field,
etc.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a compression pointer OFFSET.
requirements.required_behavior: Measure OFFSET in octets from the start of the message, with offset zero identifying the first octet of the header ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: Pointer targets at known message offsets can distinguish message-relative addressing from other bases.

requirements.quote:
The pointer takes the form of a two octet sequence:

    +--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+
    | 1  1|                OFFSET                   |
    +--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+

The first two bits are ones.  This allows a pointer to be distinguished
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a compression pointer.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the 14 bits following the two leading one bits as OFFSET, giving a representable range from 0 through 16383.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-octet pointer diagram assigns the remaining 14 bits to OFFSET; bit extraction and bounds can be checked.

requirements.quote:
The compression scheme allows a domain name in a message to be
represented as either:

   - a sequence of labels ending in a zero octet
requirements.condition: When representing a domain name in a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit a sequence of labels terminated by a zero octet.
requirements.why_checkable: A name encoded with a zero-terminated label sequence can be decoded and its boundary checked.

requirements.quote:
The compression scheme allows a domain name in a message to be
represented as either:

   - a sequence of labels ending in a zero octet

   - a pointer
requirements.condition: When representing a domain name in a message using compression.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the entire on-wire name to consist of a pointer.
requirements.why_checkable: A pointer-only name exercises a distinct permitted representation.

requirements.quote:
The compression scheme allows a domain name in a message to be
represented as either:

   - a sequence of labels ending in a zero octet

   - a pointer

   - a sequence of labels ending with a pointer
requirements.condition: When representing a domain name in a message using compression.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit a sequence of labels terminated by a pointer.
requirements.why_checkable: A name with initial labels and a pointer suffix exercises the third permitted representation.

requirements.quote:
Pointers can only be used for occurances of a domain name where the
format is not class specific.
requirements.condition: When deciding whether a domain-name occurrence may use a compression pointer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a pointer for a domain-name occurrence whose format is class specific.
requirements.why_checkable: Compression decisions can be inspected for class-specific name formats.

requirements.quote:
If a domain name is contained in a part of the message subject to a
length field (such as the RDATA section of an RR), and compression is



Mockapetris                                                    [Page 30]


RFC 1035        Domain Implementation and Specification    November 1987


used, the length of the compressed name is used in the length
calculation, rather than the length of the expanded name.
requirements.condition: When a compressed domain name is contained in a message part governed by a length field, such as RR RDATA.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the length of the compressed name in the length-field calculation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the expanded name length in that calculation.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded length field can be compared with the compressed name bytes and the expanded name size.

requirements.quote:
Programs are free to avoid using pointers in messages they generate,
although this will reduce datagram capacity, and may cause truncation.
requirements.required_behavior: Programs may avoid using compression pointers.
requirements.why_checkable: A generator that emits uncompressed names exercises the explicitly permitted choice; pointer use is not mandatory.

requirements.quote:
However all programs are required to understand arriving messages that
contain pointers.
requirements.condition: When receiving a message containing compression pointers.
requirements.required_behavior: Understand the arriving message containing compression pointers.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming compressed names can be decoded even when the program emits only uncompressed names.

the root domain name has no
labels.
requirements.condition: When representing or interpreting the root domain name.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the root domain name as having no labels.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded root can be checked for an empty label sequence.

requirements.quote:
The root domain name is

defined by a single octet of zeros at 92; the root domain name has no

requirements.condition: When encoding the root domain name without compression.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the root as one zero octet.
